response.report:
EXAM: Chest radiograph, single frontal PA view (study date not verified in findings)
CLINICAL INDICATION: Routine surveillance. History of treated breast cancer. No new symptoms.
ORDERING PROVIDER: Not available in findings
COMPARISON: Prior chest radiograph, PA (date not verified in findings)
TECHNIQUE: Current PA. Prior PA. Both adequate inspiration, no rotation. Current has slightly higher contrast and penetration than prior. Breast shadows and left chest wall soft tissues lie differently between studies. No lateral view.

LOOK AT FIRST:
- No time-sensitive findings. Priority for review per triage (urgency high, radiologist review next shift): F6 right hilar and infrahilar fullness, then F2 right lower zone interstitial markings. Both indeterminate.

FINDINGS (systematic read, done blind to the indication):
- Airway / lungs: Trachea central. Carina and main bronchi not narrowed. Lungs well inflated. No consolidation, mass or band-like collapse. Coarse linear bronchovascular markings in the right medial lower zone are more conspicuous on the current, no confluent consolidation (F2). Indeterminate, since the current exposure is higher in contrast and the breast shadow overlaps the zone differently, so technique may explain it. Both reads rated it indeterminate. A tiny dense focus projects over the right lower zone on the current and is not clearly seen on the prior. It is undetermined (see CAN'T DETERMINE).
- Mediastinum / hila: Prominent aortic knuckle consistent with an unfolded aorta, similar to prior. Upper mediastinum not widened (F3). Right hilar and infrahilar fullness and density, more conspicuous than on the prior, left hilum not enlarged (F6). Indeterminate. The two blind reads disagreed (only one read identified it), and the sharper, deeper-inspiration current film may account for part of the difference. Size change is not comparable.
- Pleura: No pleural line to suggest pneumothorax. Right costophrenic angle sharp. Left costophrenic angle appears sharp but is partly overlapped by breast shadow. No visible pleural thickening.
- Heart: Cardiac silhouette within normal limits on PA with clear borders, similar to prior (F4).
- Bones / soft tissue: No displaced rib fracture or destructive rib lesion seen at this resolution. Clavicles and shoulders intact. Mild curvature and degenerative change of the visible spine. No soft tissue gas. Left chest wall implanted venous access device with arcing tubing and a small metallic component over the left mid zone, present on both studies, no new device (F1). The catheter course and tip are not confidently traced. Upper abdomen: more gas-filled bowel loops in the left upper abdomen on the current, no free gas under either dome (F5). Indeterminate. The two blind reads disagreed (only one read identified it).

INTERVAL CHANGE:
- Changed: Right hilar and infrahilar fullness appears more conspicuous (F6, indeterminate, not comparable, reads disagreed). Right lower zone linear markings appear more conspicuous (F2, indeterminate, possibly technique-related). More left upper abdominal bowel gas (F5, indeterminate, reads disagreed). The device reservoir projects over a higher rib level on the current, but true migration cannot be judged given the soft tissue and positioning differences.
- Unchanged: Aortic knuckle and upper mediastinal width (similar). Cardiac silhouette (similar). Left chest wall implanted venous access device present on both studies, no new device. Bony appearance similar to prior.

RECIST 1.1: Not computed on radiographs.

CAN'T DETERMINE:
- Is the tiny dense focus over the right lower zone on the current a true nodule, for example a calcified granuloma, or a vessel end-on? | Reason: The focus is very small, sits among crossing vessels, and is not clearly visible on the prior, which has lower contrast. A frontal film does not separate a small nodule from a vessel end-on or a bone island. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS. If it persists, CT chest.
- Is the increased conspicuity of the right lower zone markings a true interval change? (F2) | Reason: The current image has higher contrast and a different breast shadow position, both of which make markings look more prominent. | Recommend: Correlate clinically. Short-interval repeat PA and lateral, or CT chest if there is clinical concern.
- Where is the catheter tip of the left chest wall device, and has the device moved? (F1) | Reason: The central course of the tubing is not traceable through the mediastinum at this resolution. The metallic component projects at a different rib level on the two films, which soft tissue and breast positioning might explain. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS with windowing for lines. Add a lateral view if tip position matters clinically.
- Is there a small left pleural effusion or a subtle left lower zone opacity? | Reason: Breast shadow overlaps the left costophrenic region and lower zone on both films, and there is no lateral view. | Recommend: Lateral view if clinically relevant.
- Are there subtle lesions in the ribs or spine? | Reason: The images are low resolution and compressed, so fine bone detail such as pedicles and small lucent lesions is not assessable. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS on bone settings.
- Is the right hilar and infrahilar fullness a real interval change, such as enlarged nodes or a hilar mass, or prominent vessels made more conspicuous by technique? (F6) | Reason: A frontal film alone cannot separate vessels from nodes or mass. The current is sharper and at deeper inspiration than the prior. | Recommend: CT chest with contrast. A lateral view would help if CT is not immediately available.
- Is the small dense nodular focus over the medial right lower zone on the current a true lung nodule, a calcified granuloma, or a vessel seen end-on? | Reason: It is a small focus on X-ray within crowded bronchovascular markings and breast shadow, and no definite matching focus is seen at the same site on the softer prior image. | Recommend: CT chest.
- Are the more conspicuous right lower zone linear markings a true interstitial change? (F2) | Reason: The current is sharper and slightly different in exposure and inspiration, and breast shadow overlies the region on both films. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS. If the difference persists there, CT chest.
- Where is the port catheter tip, and has the port or catheter moved? (F1) | Reason: The catheter tip cannot be traced over the mediastinum at this image resolution. The different projected level of the reservoir may reflect arm and breast position only. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS with windowing to trace the catheter to its tip. Add a lateral view if tip position remains unclear.
- Is the heterogeneous texture of the left humeral head a bone lesion or a normal or degenerative appearance? | Reason: The images are low resolution and the shoulder is at the edge of a chest film, so fine bone detail is unreliable. The appearance is similar on both studies. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS. Dedicated left shoulder radiographs if the appearance persists.

IMPRESSION:
1. Right hilar and infrahilar fullness, more conspicuous than on the prior (F6). Indeterminate. The two blind reads disagreed. Real change (enlarged nodes or mass) versus vessels accentuated by technique cannot be separated on a frontal film. In the setting of treated breast cancer, this warrants early radiologist review.
2. More conspicuous coarse linear markings in the right medial lower zone (F2). Indeterminate, possibly technique-related. No confluent consolidation.
3. Tiny dense focus over the right lower zone, undetermined (nodule versus vessel end-on).
4. More left upper abdominal bowel gas (F5). Indeterminate, reads disagreed. No free gas under either dome.
5. Left chest wall implanted venous access device present on both studies, no new device (F1). Catheter tip not traced and migration cannot be judged.
6. Stable prominent aortic knuckle with upper mediastinum not widened (F3), and cardiac silhouette within normal limits (F4).
7. No pneumothorax, no definite lung mass or confluent opacity, and no destructive rib lesion seen. The left costophrenic region is partly hidden by breast shadow, and the other items under CAN'T DETERMINE remain open, including the left humeral head texture.

RECOMMENDATIONS:
- CT chest with contrast for the right hilar fullness (F6). Interval not specified in findings. Triage calls for radiologist review next shift. Lateral view if CT is not immediately available.
- CT chest for the tiny right lower zone focus if it persists on PACS review. Interval not specified in findings.
- For the right lower zone markings (F2), review source images in PACS. Short-interval repeat PA and lateral, or CT chest if there is clinical concern or the difference persists.
- Review source images in PACS with line and bone windowing for the device tip and bone detail. Add a lateral view if tip position or the left costophrenic region matters clinically.
- Dedicated left shoulder radiographs if the left humeral head appearance persists.

AI DRAFT: requires resident review and attending signature.
